title: oist/LuscombeU_Selenoproteins_Pipeline pipeline parameters
description: Annotation of selenoprotein genes, Sec machinery and tRNA-Sec in genome assemblies

input_output_options.title: Input/output options
input_output_options.description: Define where the pipeline should find input data and save output data.

input.description: Path to comma-separated file containing information about the samples in the experiment.
input.help_text: You will need to create a design file with information about the samples in your experiment before running the pipeline. Use this parameter to specify its location. It has to be a comma-separated file with 3 columns, and a header row.

outdir.description: The output directory where the results will be saved. You have to use absolute paths to storage on Cloud infrastructure.

email.help_text: Set this parameter to your e-mail address to get a summary e-mail with details of the run sent to you when the workflow exits. If set in your user config file (`~/.nextflow/config`) then you don't need to specify this on the command line for every run.

multiqc_title.description: MultiQC report title. Printed as page header, used for filename if not otherwise specified.

selenoprotein_gene_options.title: Selenoprotein gene options
selenoprotein_gene_options.description: Options for the prediction of selenoprotein genes and their supporting evidence.

selenoprofiles_data.description: Selenoprofiles data directory or archive. If unset, the pipeline downloads it with `selenoprofiles -download`.
selenoprofiles_data.help_text: A directory written by `selenoprofiles -download`, or a directory or `.tar.gz` archive holding only the profile alignments and their `.fa.config` files. Profiles that use tag or gene-ontology filters need the full data directory.

selenoprofiles_overrides.description: Directory or `.tar.gz` archive of Selenoprofiles profiles that replace the standard profiles of the same name.
selenoprofiles_overrides.help_text: Each profile is a `<name>.fa` alignment with its `<name>.fa.config` and, optionally, `<name>.fa.profile_data`, as made by `selenoprofiles build`. A profile named like a standard one (for example `pstk`) replaces it, so that the standard profile sets (`eukarya`, `machinery`) use it; a profile with a new name is added and must be named in the `profiles` column of the samplesheet.

skip_miniprot.description: Skip the miniprot cross-check of Selenoprofiles Sec sites.

skip_secis.description: Skip the SECIS search in the 3' flanks of eukaryotic predictions.

secis_cm.description: Covariance model file for the SECIS search.
secis_cm.help_text: May contain several models. The pipeline runs cmsearch with `--cut_ga` unless `--secis_min_bits` is set, so each model needs gathering thresholds, as Rfam models have. A model built from Oikopleura dioica SECIS elements is provided: `${projectDir}/assets/secis/oikopleura_dioica_secis.cm`; use it with `--secis_min_bits`, as it has no gathering threshold.

secis_min_bits.description: Report SECIS hits from this bit score instead of using the model's gathering threshold (cmsearch -T).
secis_min_bits.help_text: Weak hits are then listed with their E-value in the gene tables; only hits that cmsearch includes (E-value of 0.01 or less) count as SECIS support in the summary.

trnasec_options.title: tRNA-Sec options
trnasec_options.description: Options for the prediction of selenocysteine tRNA genes.

trnasec_tools.description: Comma-separated tRNA-Sec tools to run: secmarker, cmsearch, trnascanse.
trnasec_tools.help_text: Loci found by two or more tools count as supported in the Sec trait call. tRNAscan-SE is off by default: Debian distributes it in non-free because of one source file.

trnasec_cm.description: Covariance model file for the tRNA-Sec search with cmsearch, which uses `--cut_ga`.

annotation_check_options.title: Annotation check options
annotation_check_options.description: Checks of the reference annotation given in the samplesheet's annotation column (GFF3 with mRNA, exon and CDS features).

readthrough_screen.description: Screen all annotated transcripts for TGA codons at the edges or inside of their CDS, ranked by the SECIS score of their 3' UTR.
readthrough_screen.help_text: Finds selenoprotein genes whose annotated protein starts after the Sec codon, ends at it, or translates it as X. Needs exon features in the annotation.

screen_cm.description: Covariance model for the transcript screen; defaults to `--secis_cm`.
screen_cm.help_text: The screen reports hits of 10 bits or more, so models without gathering thresholds, such as `${projectDir}/assets/secis/oikopleura_dioica_secis.cm`, can be used.

expectation_options.title: Expectation options
expectation_options.description: Compare the Sec sites found with an expected selenoproteome.

expectation.help_text: An entry for Oikopleura is provided: `${projectDir}/assets/expectations/oikopleura_dioica.csv` (lineage `Oikopleura`). Counts are compared per family.

expectation_lineage.description: Row of the expectation table to use, e.g. `Oikopleura`.

expectation_copies.description: Expected copies of each gene, e.g. 2 for a diploid assembly with both haplotypes.

expectation_hemizygous.description: Comma-separated families counted once whatever `--expectation_copies`, e.g. `TXNRD,SELENOT` for the X-specific region of male O. dioica assemblies.

institutional_config_options.title: Institutional config options
institutional_config_options.description: Parameters used to describe centralised config profiles. These should not be edited.
institutional_config_options.help_text: The centralised nf-core configuration profiles use a handful of pipeline parameters to describe themselves. This information is then printed to the Nextflow log when you run a pipeline. You should not need to change these values when you run a pipeline.

custom_config_version.description: Git commit id for Institutional configs.

custom_config_base.help_text: If you're running offline, Nextflow will not be able to fetch the institutional config files from the internet. If you don't need them, then this is not a problem. If you do need them, you should download the files from the repo and tell Nextflow where to find them with this parameter.

generic_options.title: Generic options
generic_options.description: Less common options for the pipeline, typically set in a config file.
generic_options.help_text:
These options are common to all nf-core pipelines and allow you to customise some of the core preferences for how the pipeline runs.

Typically these options would be set in a Nextflow config file loaded for all pipeline runs, such as `~/.nextflow/config`.

publish_dir_mode.description: Method used to save pipeline results to output directory.
publish_dir_mode.help_text: The Nextflow `publishDir` option specifies which intermediate files should be saved to the output directory. This option tells the pipeline what method should be used to move these files. See [Nextflow docs](https://www.nextflow.io/docs/latest/process.html#publishdir) for details.

email_on_fail.description: Email address for completion summary, only when pipeline fails.
email_on_fail.help_text: An email address to send a summary email to when the pipeline is completed - ONLY sent if the pipeline does not exit successfully.

plaintext_email.description: Send plain-text email instead of HTML.

max_multiqc_email_size.description: File size limit when attaching MultiQC reports to summary emails.

monochrome_logs.description: Do not use coloured log outputs.

multiqc_config.description: Custom config file to supply to MultiQC.

multiqc_logo.description: Custom logo file to supply to MultiQC. File name must also be set in the MultiQC config file

multiqc_methods_description.description: Custom MultiQC yaml file containing HTML including a methods description.

validate_params.description: Boolean whether to validate parameters against the schema at runtime

pipelines_testdata_base_path.description: Base URL or local path to location of pipeline test dataset files

trace_report_suffix.description: Suffix to add to the trace report filename. Default is the date and time in the format yyyy-MM-dd_HH-mm-ss.

help_full.description: Display the full detailed help message.

show_hidden.description: Display hidden parameters in the help message (only works when --help or --help_full are provided).
